youtube.title: GREENWASHED
youtube.summary: Jaspreet Boparai and Don Nicolson discuss the IPCC’s decision to exclude the SSP5-8.5 emissions scenario from future assessments and argue that worst-case climate assumptions remain embedded in New Zealand infrastructure planning. They focus on South Dunedin flood mitigation proposals, consultant involvement, insurance implications and Ministry for the Environment guidance. Jaspreet contends that climate risk modelling has created a self-reinforcing system benefiting large engineering firms and insurers, while Don argues governments should revisit policies driving rising costs for ratepayers and taxpayers. youtube.title: LESLIE MANOOKIAN
youtube.summary: Leslie Manookian, founder of the Health Freedom Defense Fund, discusses the U.S. Supreme Court's refusal to hear a challenge to Covid-era vaccine mandates, strengthening government authority over personal medical choices. She outlines efforts to advance Medical Freedom Act legislation in multiple states and cites polling she says shows strong public support for informed consent. Leslie also raises concerns about digital IDs, data centres, AI infrastructure and surveillance systems and expanding state control over our lives. For everything you need to Say No to Digital ID For further information: HFD: The Supreme Court's refusal to consider bodily autonomy is a disgrace HFD: The Medical Freedom Act Coalition sees successes sweep across the nation HFD: Data center construction boom an ominous sign Children's Health Defense Arizona: A united stand to protect homeopathy Discover Leslie Manookian on X

youtube.title: LEITH VAN ONSELEN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Leith van Onselen, chief economist at MB Fund and co-founder of MacroBusiness, about signs that Australia's long property boom may be ending. Leith argues Sydney and Melbourne are leading a housing correction that could become the largest in 40 years, driven by higher interest rates, tax changes, weakening confidence and falling auction clearance rates. For more information visit MacroBusiness or find them on X and YouTube

youtube.title: HOLLY LAWFORD-SMITH
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with University of Melbourne political philosopher Holly Lawford-Smith about the state of free speech in Australia, high-profile legal cases involving gender identity and women's spaces and growing concerns over hate speech laws and academic culture. They discuss activism, feminism, ideological conformity on university campuses, and Holly's book Feminism Beyond Left and Right . You can find Holly on her website , YouTube and X For Holly's book Feminism Beyond Left and Right

youtube.title: NEIL JOHNSTONE
youtube.summary: South Dunedin has for years been touted as the front line of the battle against climate change in New Zealand. But is it really a climate catastrophe? Or is the real issue a pipes' problem that has been known since the 1960s? Retired Otago Catchment Board and Otago Regional Council flood engineer, Neil Johnstone says it's the latter – in his words, “It's not a climate change problem, it's a catchment problem”. For more information South Dunedin Flooding – History of Council Neglect – Report – 3-6-26

youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Farzin Irani joins Paul Brennan for this week’s edition of Money Talks. They discuss competing theories about the conflicts in Iran and Russia/Ukraine and global energy markets. Irani says investors should focus less on proving grand narratives and more on protecting wealth. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. Farzin has updated his website with free resources to help people prepare for the future Discover more from Farzin on Linktr.ee

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart discuss the Gell-Mann Amnesia Effect and the collapse of trust in legacy media, arguing that many people now turn to alternative sources while risking new echo chambers. They explore social media algorithms, censorship, advertiser influence and the changing culture within journalism. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X For more information: Riding Shotgun: A Case of Media Amnesia Ian Wishart Website NY Post Tulsi Gabbard / Antony Fauci article The Real Antony Fauci Book Michael Campbell's RCR Interview with Peter Williams ABC Rejects Sall Grover's opinion piece Sall Grover X Post RNZ: Mathew Hooton appointed editor of The Post

youtube.title: SUE MIDDLETON
youtube.summary: Emeritus Professor Sue Middleton joins Maree Buscke to discuss her support for the Definition of Woman and Man Amendment Bill and why she believes biological sex remains an essential legal category. Drawing on decades of work in education, women's studies and sexuality, Middleton argues that sex and gender identity are distinct concepts and warns that confusion between them has implications for women's rights, statistics, language and public policy. For more information: Read Sue's article in the Waikato Times: Why New Zealand Law needs clear definitions of man and woman, June 11 2026 Check out Sue's website Read the Feminist Older Women Lobbyists (FOWL) submission to the Law commission on proposed changes to the Human Rights Act

youtube.title: JO GALER
youtube.summary: Following the release of plans to alleviate South Dunedin’s flooding problems with parks, canals and managed retreat, South Dunedin has become the poster-child for climate change adaptation. But residents, city councillors and flood engineers have also come forward with reports that the planners have been ignoring evidence that the real problem is an infrastructure one. In this interview, RCR’s Alistair Harding talks to Dunedin City Councillor, Jo Galer who says the process has lacked transparency and appears pre-determined. For more information check out: South Dunedin Flooding – History of Council Neglect – Report – 3-6-26

youtube.title: RODNEY’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide looks through his latest mailbag, beginning with reactions to interviews with Sarah and Randall Farrant and Gary Moller, including debate over Gary’s description of Chile. Listeners also praise Rodney’s empathy and interviewing style. Much of the discussion centres on Ashley Church’s book Prophecy Shock , with correspondents offering differing interpretations of biblical prophecy, Israel and the end times. Text your feedback to 2057 or email inbox@rcr.media

youtube.title: ALLAN BEEVER
youtube.summary: Professor Allan Beever of Auckland University of Technology joins Paul Brennan to discuss why New Zealand faces a pivotal moment as the post-war world gives way to a more complex multipolar order. He argues that Wellington has yet to develop a clear strategy for balancing its traditional ties with the United States against growing economic links with China and emerging powers. Discover more from Allan on YouTube

youtube.title: MICHAEL CAMPBELL
youtube.summary: Veteran broadcaster Peter Williams catches up with US Open Golf Champion Michael Campbell, who famously won holding off Tiger Woods in 2005. Campbell opens up candidly about developing atrial fibrillation after his second Moderna vaccine and his deep frustration that no one in government or the pharmaceutical industry has accepted responsibility. He is also highly critical of the mainstream media for perpetuating misinformation about the vaccine. Keep up to date and sign up for Bites News

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by Tim Wilms to discuss Australia’s first H5N1 bird flu cases and growing public scepticism toward media warnings. They discuss possible impacts of the government response on poultry. They also discuss Pauline Hanson’s “Fire the Liar” campaign, protests surrounding her events and her National Press Club speech. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled

youtube.title: UNDER THE HOOD
youtube.summary: On Under the Hood , Graham ‘Hoody' Hood reflects on why people can become trapped in destructive patterns, whether in relationships, resentment or unhealthy ways of thinking. Drawing on a powerful experience from his days as an outback pilot, he explores how familiarity with pain can make freedom difficult to embrace. Hoody argues that healing, forgiveness and personal responsibility are essential to rebuilding families, communities and nations, urging listeners to stop living in the past and choose a more hopeful path forward. Discover more from Hoody at Club Grubbery or find him on Facebook and X

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan shares listener reactions to interviews covering Wellington's water reforms, roadside drug testing, Robert Muldoon, weather warnings, council spending and international affairs. Listeners reflect on nostalgia for a more unified New Zealand, concerns about bureaucracy and national sovereignty and frustration with what they see as excessive government intervention.
